articleTitle: The effect of the continuous energy efficient upgrading of LED street lighting technology: The case study of Egnatia Odos
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: With the advent of LED technology, lighting studies have gained a great interest, especially street lighting. Nowadays, these studies demonstrate the great energy savings achieved by replacing high pressure sodium lamps with LED. As LED technology is continuously improving, energy savings are increased and thus the payback time of the investment is decreasing more and more. However, there are a lot of cases were the public constructions are delayed and the initial lighting design is getting obsolete, due to the energy efficient upgrade of the LEDs. In this research a newest version (2019) for the lighting design was performed using the latest technology of LED street lighting and compared with the one performed in 2017. Egnatia Odos EO, the largest national road in Greece, was selected as the case study for both studies (2017 and 2019). EO covers a distant of 670 km in northern Greece. Existing lighting infrastructure was designed and installed 17 years before, according to the previous version of EN12301 [1] -[3].

articleTitle: Dimming of street lighting systems with current reactive energy control
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The report analyzes the behavior of the lighting load for street lighting during dimming. There are classical installations with HLVH and new - with LED lights. For both types of equipment, the power factor becomes worse when dimmed - when dimming from 100 to 50% for the first 0.95> PF> 0.6; for the second -0.96> PF> -0.8. And if in the first case the increase in the price of active energy is not high (sanctions in percent of the so-called cosine-fi tariff if PF <; 0.9), in the case of the second type the reactive energy is sold by the electricity distribution companies at the same cost as the active. The question is how to prevent the payment of reactive energy as active?

articleTitle: Modelling the Thermal Conditions of a LED Lamp
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: An analysis of the construction of the LED lamp has been performed in order to estimate the energy input and output flows. A model of the thermal conditions of a LED lamp has been suggested in this paper. A specialized software application was developed, which implements the created algorithms. Simulation experiments were performed and compared with the experimental data. The obtained results showed very good match between the modeled and experimentally obtained values.

articleTitle: Rehabilitation and Remote Control of Municipalities Street Lighting
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: For road/street lighting in the EU, Regulation 245/2009 applies. A major problem after the rehabilitation of street lighting systems under the EC Operational Programs is the monitoring of the EU green public procurement criteria (EU GPPC). These criteria cover three main sections: energy consumption, light pollution and life cycle costing of the installations. The paper examines the possibilities for rehabilitation of public lighting in the municipalities of the Republic of Bulgaria, the technologies for the construction of the transmission environment and the devices that monitor and manage the public lighting by regions.

articleTitle: The LED spectral power distribution modelled by different functions - how spectral matching quality affected computed LED color parameters
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The paper is describing different alternatives for mathematical modelling of LED's spectral power distribution. Gaussians, logistic power peak and asymmetric double sigmoidal functions are tested with different shape and peak wavelength LEDs. Article shows how SPD accuracy modeling is affecting color quality parameters and luminous efficiency of LED. Consequences of applying always single SPD model for different LED emitters are shown for chosen parameters.

articleTitle: Annual use of luminaire groups for the entrance area according to the orientation of the road tunnel
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Annual use of luminaire groups for the entrance area according to the orientation of the road tunnel; Angel Pachamanov, Borislav Pregyov, Kiril Kassev. Adaptation tunnel lighting is performed with three or four groups of luminaires switched on or off when increasing or decreasing the adaptation brightness. The dependence between the operating power of the lighting and the duration of turning on the individual groups of luminaires varies with the different orientation of the tunnel portal. It is nonlinear, therefore the modes of operation and dimming of the groups of luminaires are determined by the so-called orderly schedule of adaptation brightness. It gives the frequency of occurrence of set values of adaptation brightness in the annual plan. For each orientation at the tunnel entrance, the ordered schedule is different, which is why the dimming mode of the luminaires from the available groups is different.

articleTitle: Harmonic pollutions generated by industrial lighting systems
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The report presents a study of the harmonic pollution of the power grid generated by industrial LED lighting. A specific industrial room was investigated, for which the parameters of the electrical grid for continuous operation were measured. A high precision network analyzer was used to determine the higher harmonics generated as a result of the use of LED light sources. The relevant conclusions and conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Influence of the angle of fall of light on the photovoltaic panel and its optimization - literature review
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Scarce energy sources in today’s world are the cause of meeting energy needs in everyday life through renewable energy sources. Concerns about climate change, rising oil prices and increased government subsidies lead to enlarged investments in renewable energy sources. Today, research focuses on optimizing and improving efficiency of these sources. Renewable energy is derived from natural processes that are constantly renewed. In most of its forms it is delivered directly from the sun or from the heat accumulated in the earth. The purpose of this publication is to present a realistic approach to enhancing efficiency in cases where green energy is extracted from sun through photovoltaic panels. This would lead to a higher power supply for artificial lighting.There are significant energy losses when installing a solar panel on a static structure in the morning and late afternoon due to the fact that the panel is not sun-oriented in east-west direction (daily sun motion). There are losses also when the solar panel is not perpendicular to sun rays (in north-south direction). This publication presents the influence of the sunlight angle falling on photovoltaics and its optimization.

articleTitle: LED Luminaire Optical Lens Optimization for Road Lighting Designed According to Luminance Requirement
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: A methodology for iterative optimization of optical systems for street LED luminaires intended for roads designed according to luminance requirement is proposed in the paper. The methodology comprises the following stages: iterative change of the shape of secondary lens of a computer model of the optical system, photometric analysis using the Monte Carlo raytracing method of the modelled three-dimensional optical systems to calculate their photometric characteristics, optimal road lighting calculations with an optimum criterion - maximum luminaire spacing meeting the requirements of standard for the selected M6 lighting class of the road, through the analysis of which the optimal solution is found.

articleTitle: Investigating the Influence of Environmental and Design Parameters on the Thermal Regime of a LED Lamp
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The increase of the LED's temperature above a certain threshold decreases significantly their live expectancy. Therefore, it is important to investigate LEDs' thermal regime during the design process in different conditions for exploitation. The influence of the construction and the environment parameters on the thermal regime of LED lamp was investigated in this paper. The study was done with a specially developed software, based on a model, describing the thermal regime of LED lamps. Next, a methodology for the research has been developed and a simulation study was carried out. The results of this investigation are represented graphically.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Computer Modeling of Secondary Lens for Street LED Luminaire in AutoCAD
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: In the paper is proposed methodology for iterative three-dimensional computer modeling of secondary optical lenses for street LED luminaires by using of Photopia and AutoCAD software. The methodology allows achieving of various desired light distributions of the luminaires by iteratively modifying the three-dimensional shape of the secondary lens. The created three-dimensional models of optical lenses shown are tested by Monte Carlo raytracing photometric analysis. The results confirm the performance and the possibilities for application of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Considerations on disturbances in the electrical supply network caused by LEDs light projectors
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: In the first part of this paper, the authors present the results of the luminotechnical calculations based on the reconstruction of the photometric curves of a LEDs projector PREMIUM LUX LED 38dgr type. Thus by using the equal plane angles method, the emitted total luminous flux and the efficiency of this luminaire were determined. Then was analysed the illuminance's distribution in the horizontal and vertical plane, at different heights and the rectangular surface illuminated by the considered luminaire. In the second part of the paper is presented the analysis of disturbances in the electrical supply network caused by this type of LEDs light projectors. In this regard the test report, provided by a harmonic and flicker analyzer, Type HAR 1000-1P (EMC Partner AG Switzerland) was used. The results of the measurements were interpreted, making observations regarding harmonic current emissions, voltage fluctuations and flicker indicators.

Author Keywords: disturbances in the electrical supply network

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Luminaire for Use in Science and Education Establishments
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: A special purpose LED luminaire has been developed for use in science and education establishments. This paper describes the test and assembly of the developed LED luminaire. Based on measurements the light and electrical parameters have been determined to meet the requirements for luminaire installations in this type of establishments.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of the Reflective Properties of Façade Materials for Architectural Lighting Design
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The paper presents a detailed feasibility study carried out before the design stage of the architectural lighting of the building of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering. The reflectance coefficients of all the surfaces of the building are measured and statistically verified. The bidirectional reflectance distribution functions of three basic surfaces are also measured. The color coordinates of the surfaces are matched to the color coordinates of the light of the flood lights chosen for realization of the lighting concept.

articleTitle: Training stand with control systems for street, tunnel and industrial lighting
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The report examines the real-world lighting systems of the TU-Sofia lighting laboratory, which will demonstrate to future lighting designers three types of special lighting systems and their management. In street lighting, an option for remote control of rehabilitated street systems is shown. With the tunnelighting system implemented, the two gates are not connected to each other and are monitored directly via the global network. The same system, with minor modifications, is also used to control the lighting of industrial halls on the luminance of the windows.

articleTitle: Energy efficient biodynamic lighting for use in science and education establishments
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: An LED luminaire has been developed for use in science and education establishments. Four of the assembled luminaires were installed in study hall 12541 of Technical University of Sofia. The new lighting installation replaces four luminaire with fluorescent lamps T8 with output power 136W each. The paper describes a comparison of the light and technical performance of both installations. A realistic 3D model of the study hall was created to determine the performance of the new installation and the light reflectance coefficients value of all used surfaces and materials was measured. After physical implementation of the new luminaires, light performance measurements were taken in accordance to standard EN 12464-1 "Lighting of work places - Part 1: Indoor work places".

articleTitle: Island photovoltaic tunnel lighting systems
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Due to the direct correlation between the external illumination in front of the tunnel and the illumination inside the tunnel, road tunnels are possibly the most favorable consumer of electricity produced by photovoltaic (PVS) systems located near their portals. Thus saving the cost of energy supply which are around 30% of its price. The operation of anPVS in an island regime also saves costs for the connection of PVS to the grid of the electricity distribution company. The report takes into account the peculiarities of the operation of the PVSs as an island, justifying the benefit of constructing them as portal shading facilities over the road in front of the tunnel entrance. This reduces the installed power for daylight, respectively the investment for PVS.

articleTitle: Statistical methods for forecasting the expense of electrical energy
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: An energy audit with prescriptions of energy saving measures for the educational buildings of University of Food Technology (UFT) - Plovdiv was done. When creating a system for collecting, archiving and processing the energy expenses, it is important the costs incurred to be analyzed. The mathematical statistics gives an appropriate tool for this. The analysis showed that much of the cost is due to the building's lighting. In this approach, a forecast for future costs of electrical energy can be done with a sufficient number of accumulated data.

articleTitle: Image-Based Automated Hit Detection and Score Calculation on a Steel Dartboard
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: This paper presents an approach for implementing an automated hit detection and score calculation system for a steel dartboard using a standard webcam. First, the rectilinear field separations of the dartboard are described mathematically by means of line slopes and are than stored. These slopes serve as a basis for later score calculation. In addition, thrown darts have to be detected and the pixel at which the dart cuts the dartboard has to be determined. When this information is known, a comparison is made using the line slopes, allowing the field number of the hit to be detected. The decision for single, double or triple hit is made by evaluating the defined colors on the dartboard. All these functions are then packaged in a Matlab GUI.

articleTitle: Measurement systems used in measuring the illuminance of the road
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Street lighting is one of the elements of road infrastructure that affects safety. Therefore, the important issue is the verification of the street lighting condition in the context of fulfilling the normative requirements. The currently used method of measuring road illumination with the use of handheld meter is labour-intense and time-consuming, as a result of which the street lighting audit is neglected. An alternative method of measurement is the measurement systems located on the vehicle. The publication presents the methods used in the measuring of the illuminance of road. Attention is paid to the disadvantages of the commonly used static method and an alternative is presented by using mobile systems to measure the lighting condition on the road. Authors presented a change in the concept of measuring systems built over the years, including own concept implemented with the results of pilot studies.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency and Economic aspects of Lighting
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Currently the world is suffering from many issues as global warming and emission of green house gasses, is known as hazardous once, therefore it is in the lime light of international organizations and focus which makes it to be one of the most crucial issue around the world. Energy efficiency, Lighting techniques and lighting accessories play a vital rule both in the terms of global warming and as well energy saving which leads it to economic efficiency of lighting, its benefits and impacts on both aspects, whether economic side or environmental issues. The paper will be based on two issues which are energy efficiency and economic aspects of lighting. A general overview will be given about energy efficiency, its benefits, tips, and economic aspects of energy efficiency while for economic aspects of lighting will be illustrated specifically that how with energy saving techniques and less energy consumption luminaries, lighting can bring changes in both economic and environmental aspects.

articleTitle: Energy Costs Reduce in Energy-Efficient Buildings by Applying Single Axis Solar Tracker
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Different ways to increase the energy efficiency of buildings are constantly sought [1-5]. Green electricity use is the perfect logical addition to an energy efficient building. Such electricity can be obtained from sunlight using a photovoltaic panel. Most photovoltaic panels have a CPA approximately 20%, reached at 25°C. It means that at the outlet on the panel surface the transformed electrical energy is maximum 20% of the solar energy. The panel should have a temperature 25°C and be perpendicular to the sun's rays in order to use all of the panel's capabilities. These conditions can be achieved with a sun monitoring system. That publication reveals the creation of such a system.

articleTitle: Examination of the Dynamic Variation of the Color Homogeneity of the Emitted Light from a Linear LED Luminaire with a Dynamic Color Adjustment of the Light
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: A detailed study of the space uniformity of color distribution from LED luminaire with “tunable white” light is presented in a regime of dimming from 100% to 1%. The results of this work will be the base for detailed research work on the influence of this lighting on human wellbeing.

articleTitle: Optimizing the levels of group dimming of luminaires for adaptation tunnel lighting
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: When dimming tunnel LED luminaires, the efficiency of the drivers decreases as the dimming depth increases - the relative losses in the power driver are greatest at the lowest flow rate (36% loss at 10% F/Fnom, 17% at 20% F/Fnom, 11% at 40% F/Fnom, 8% at 70% F/Fnom, 6.5% at 100% F/Fnom). Obviously, with the presence of several groups of luminaires, the number of luminaires in the group and the dimming levels of the luminaires of each group are obtained by solving an optimization task. In the report, an optimization task has been formulated and solved for specific tunnel entrance exposures with corresponding ordered luminance schedules L20. The target function is a minimum power loss in the drivers used at a given time flow schedule of the luminance L20.

articleTitle: An adaptive system for quality improved digitalization of medical images
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Medical images are an important part of the modern diagnostic process of many diseases. The low quality of images is one of the reasons for hypo- or hyper-diagnosis as a result of incorrect deciphering. One of the image applications is to track changes in patients' organs and tissues over time. Screen-films and direct exposure films are part of medical image sources. The proposed paper presents a prototype of a new generation of medical image fil digitizer. The characteristics of such an apparatus and the necessary technologies for its implementation are considered.

articleTitle: Estimation of the uncertainty in measurement of light distribution of luminaires by means of telecentric photometer
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The paper shows the methodology for estimation of the calibration uncertainty of a telecentric photometer. It shows in details all the possible sources of uncertainty that should be considered in a photometrical measurement, according to the construction of the equipment. In order to verify the experimental results, a verification has also been carried out - the light distribution of the test luminaire has also been measured with a previously calibrated mirror distributive gonio photometer.

articleTitle: Artistic and Architectural Lighting of the Building of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering of Technical University of Sofia, Bulgaria
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The paper presents the architectural and artistic concept for the lighting of the faculty of Electrical engineering of the Technical University of Sofia - Bulgaria. Except for the simulation model of the architectural lighting of the building, a lot of experiments and preconditions are made. All the surfaces of the building are experimentally tested and their reflective properties are obtained. Test flood lights are chosen according to the reflectance of the surfaces and their color characteristics are experimentally tested. Based on these experimental results, on site experiments are also made and after that the whole idea of the architectural lighting of the twelfth educational building of TU Sofia is simulated. The simulation gives an idea very close to the night look of the building (if the concept is accepted and realized), based on the real characteristics of surfaces and luminaires.

articleTitle: Influence of the Position of LED Luminaires on their Thermal Regimes in Photometrical Measurements with a Telecentric Photometer
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The current paper shows experimentally obtained results for the heating of a LED luminaire put in different burning positions during photometric measurements. Two different goniophotometers are considered - telecentric, where the light distribution of the luminaire is measured while the luminaire is positioned with the light sources facing up (this is not its prescribed burning position) and mirror distributive gonio photometer (MDGP), where the light distribution is measured while the luminaire is in its prescribed burning position. The first equipment has the advantage, that although the luminaire is not in its burning position, the measurement is much faster than when MDGP is used, so the thermal regime of the luminaire under consideration remains normal.

articleTitle: Zero Voltage Switch DC/DC Resonant Converter for LED Lighting Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: In the current paper a zero voltage switch DC/DC resonant converter for LED application is proposed. The mathematical model is described with differential equations.

articleTitle: Application of HEVs for Smart Home
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: In the current paper an application of the hybrid electric vehicles as a system for supplying of a smart home is presented. This solution allows a better energy management. A main characteristics of a HEVs, smart home, types of batteries and PV systems are proposed.

articleTitle: Computer Investigation of SEPIC DC-DC Converter for LED Lighting Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: In the current paper a mathematical modelling of SEPIC DC-DC converter is presented. A methodology with switching function is used. The realized model is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink environment. An optimization procedure for determination of the optimal value for the proposed solution is used. This model is suitable for a LED lighting applications.

articleTitle: Parametric Lighting Design
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Lighting a space serves not only purely functional purposes like making objects visible but also purposes which have to do more with impression and aesthetics. In most cases, the procedure of lighting design for achieving certain visual effects is still carried out empirically. Procedures or algorithms that could offer a “reverse engineering” way of lighting design i.e. algorithms that take specific visual objectives as input and give optimum lighting design solutions as output could help a lot the lighting designers to do their job more easily and efficiently.This text includes a literature review of the research on lighting design parameters and how they can be methodically controlled to attain specific visual objectives, and a presentation of a proposal for the parameterization of specific visual effects and linking it with corresponding parameters of lighting design, with the goal of arriving at more automated lighting design techniques.

articleTitle: Study on the theory of electromagnetic energy propagation through an electromagnetic wave
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The propagation of electromagnetic energy through electromagnetic waves is a complex process. Its theoretical study is based on the fundamental physical scientific laws of conservation of energy and of electrodynamics. The objective of research in the present study is to possibly improve the explanations of composite physical phenomena and to specify their parameters and characteristics.

articleTitle: Biologically active luminaire with four LEDs
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Nowadays we all know that lighting has a significant influence on human beings. And we know that influence can be positive and negative. With thoughtful lighting design and choosing the appropriate luminaires, it is possible to maximize positive effects and minimize negative effects. When we are talking about appropriate luminaries, we are having in mind biologically active luminaire with tuneable spectra. Biologically active luminaire is intended to improve the quality of life for people who spend most of the day exposed to artificial lighting. With changing correlated colour temperature and light intensity and with a sufficient amount of blue light, it is possible to affect biological processes in the human body.

articleTitle: Light Pollution – “Borders” of Lighting Design
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: History, especially the latest, shows that every human activity is in a state of development. At a certain point however, that development begins to move out from the socially acceptable norms. Often the developing process of lighting technology passes the reasonable limits. The megalomania manifests itself in the light sctattering and the uncontrolled overlit areas of the natural environment and the inner spaces. The question that still arises at present is when the average citizen and the representatives of lighting industry will identify the existence of light pollution and visual glare as harm rather than a benefit. Visual culture is educated through the realization of adequate lighting environment. Several campaigns wake up and focus public attention and awareness on the light pollution issue and its impact. The benefit of those campaigns does not relate to their demonstrational manner, but to the lack of adequate energy and environmental culture that should corresponds to the present high-technological progress. It is necessary to rethink the artificial light, the understanding of the hygiene of lighting, especially if it is overdosed and unsatisfactorily managed. Aren't we on the verge of a new lighting technical age?

articleTitle: Photovoltaic roof systems for educational buildings
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: A roof photovoltaic system (PVS) for power supply to a university building is being considered. The large roof areas of these buildings make it possible to fully meet the needs of electricity and a large part of the heat demand during the heating season. During the autumn-winter season, electricity from the PV system is used to charge the rechargeable battery (RB) for lighting and to supply air-water heat pumps to the heating installation. The electricity produced during the spring-summer season is sold to the energy system. The funds received cover a large part of winter heating costs. A small lithium-ion RB is provided to align the daily load schedule. The proposed model provides minimum energy costs annually and is planned to be implemented as a training center at TU-Sofia under OPIC Operational Program, proposal “Optimization of operating costs of building lighting and heating through the use of renewable energy sources”.

articleTitle: Urban lighting in historic settlements: from quality lighting to cultural reinforcement
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: The purpose of the study is to define the lighting design techniques and strategies that can be used in small-scale historic urban settlements in order to achieve quality lighting, cultural reinforcement and tourist attraction. By the definition of small-scale settlements this research refers to the historical centers of the city, around which the modern urban environment has been developed. Their role in urban life is analyzed by focusing on the medieval fortification settlements of the Cycladic islands as they constitute a very special case of study with strong architectural and cultural features.

articleTitle: Ray-tracing based channel modeling for the simulation of the performance of visible light communication in an indoor environment
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Ray-tracing based channel modeling is a powerful tool for the determination of the channel characteristics of VLC settings. In order to overcome the huge computational effort that is necessary in this regard, new strategies for less time-consuming ray-tracing based channel models are essential. Here we introduce a channel model that is based on optical simulations using non-sequential ray-tracing in combination with selfdeveloped algorithms in MATLAB. In addition, we discuss an approach, which allows for a time-effective determination of the dependence of the receiver position on the VLC characteristics along the diagonal of the floor of a room. Raytracing information of each ray impinging on a diagonal stripe (with a width of $\sim1.41$ cm) is exported to MATLAB for further analysis. By doing so, 26 different receiver positions along the diagonal axis of a room can be investigated using only one raytracing simulation run instead of repeating ray-tracing simulations for each of the 26 receiver positions. The error made by this simulation approach turns out to be negligible because of the small ratio between the area or the receiver stripe and the area of the whole floor.

articleTitle: Improving quality of digital medical images
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: Medical images are an important part of the modern diagnostic process of many diseases. The low quality of images is one of the reasons for hypo- or hyper-diagnosis as a result of incorrect deciphering. The proposed paper presents an extended version of our method for image quality enhancement based on the creation of a model of pseudo lighting. The method uses a single digital medical image to create a set of images by simulation different patient exposure conditions. This set of images is used to create our pseudo luminance model. In the final stage, the model is used to create a medical image with enhanced quality without medical artifacts.

articleTitle: A Lighting Proposal for A Library Project in Terms of Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 Second Balkan Junior Conference on Lighting (Balkan Light Junior)
abstract: This paper aims to achieve visual comfort conditions with less energy consumption at a university library. In this regard, a lighting design project is proposed for BUU faculty of architecture library which is an additional unit to the existing building in the pre-design phase and planning to be implemented. In this scope, artificial lighting results and daylighting availability of the library space is analyzed with a lighting simulation tool. Accordingly, solar gains were examined and the annual energy loads were calculated depending on a variety of façade shading configurations via a building energy simulation program.
